newsitem.title: JAPAN: JNR Corp land seen selling for around 240 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: JNR Corp land seen selling for around 240 bln yen.

text.p: Five tracts of prime land in Tokyo to be auctioned by the JNR Settlement Corp on Friday afternoon are expected to fetch a total of around 240 billion yen, analysts said.
The land covers 53,000 sq metres located near a central railway station in southern Tokyo and was once owned by the now-defunct Japanese National Railways.
Auction results will be announced at 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT).
JNR Settlement Corp said 39 consortiums were bidding for the tracts of land, with four groups bidding for all five tracts.
Analysts said they believe real estate developers, major car manufacturers, telecommunications firms, trading firms and at least one foreign group are among the bidders.
They said they expected the land auction to go reasonably well following the successful auction of three tracts of land near Ginza, Tokyo's premier shopping district, in early February.
The land sold for a total of 372.3 billion yen, exceeding expectations of about 300 billion yen.
"The last auction went well and sentiment in the real estate market has taken a turn for the better," said an analyst at a major domestic securities house.
One analyst was more cautious, saying that the price per square metre looked like it would be lower than expected. He forecast a total price tag of around 180 billion yen.
Others said the price would depend largely on the allowed plot ratio for development.

"The buildings in that area have a plot ratio of around 800 percent so a ratio of 1000 percent is probable," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage who expected the land to sell for between 240 and 270 billion yen.
